english: Tell me (a story about) a wolf. A wolf lived near the village. It watched the sheep at night. The shepherd's dog protected them. Now the wolf left and did not come again. I loved that dog.
uncertain: wénHm̥ read as AOR 1SG of wenH- 'love, desire' ('I loved / I came to love')

english: The sun came out here. Is it warm at your house? You are not a house to me (intended: I have no house). I have not seen the sun. Tell me about your sun. It is warm, and the birds sing.
uncertain: dṓm moy ne h₁ési: h₁ési is 2SG 'you are'; 'I have no house' needs 3SG h₁ésti -- looks like a person error
mélh₃t read as AOR of melh₃- 'come forth, appear'
sóh₂wl̥ ne dedórḱh₂e read as PRF 1SG 'I have not seen the sun' (sóh₂wl̥ as neuter ACC)

english: Sing me a song. Listen, dear one! The sun came out, and the birds sing. The day (is) warm, and the heart rejoiced. This song gives me joy. Now sing!
uncertain: léwbʰe read as VOC 'dear one, beloved'
dinós gʷʰermós: read as NOM.SG 'the day (is) warm'; the accent dinós is odd for an o-stem with root accent elsewhere (dinóy)

english: It dawned. I woke early. Why did you wake early? The birds sang. The birds greet (praise) the dawn. Now cook something. I drink water.
uncertain: h₂wést read as AOR 3SG of h₂wes- 'dawn, light up'
wédos as 'water' (ACC) is unexpected: the inherited word is the neuter r/n stem wódr̥; wédos may be a lexicon s-stem variant

english: How do I say (it)? It is snowing. -- It is snowing. Say it to your sister! The snow lies on the road. We have come into winter (or: winter has come). Do not slip on the path!
uncertain: ǵʰéyōm gʷegʷóme: PRF 1PL 'we have come' with winter as goal; English may be 'winter has come'

english: My brother laughed today. Why did he laugh? I fell (sank) into the water. Were you struck/cold? I was, and we got home safely. Together we (two) laughed.
uncertain: ḱósmi dinóy read as 'on this day' = today
séngʷm̥ (no aspirate) read as AOR 1SG of sengʷ- 'sink', not sengʷʰ- 'sing'
stéwd- sense unknown to me (cold? frightened? struck?)
nésomedʰh₂ looks 1PL middle ('we returned home safely') against 1SG stéwdm̥ -- possible person switch
sméyih₁tom read as 3DU 'the two laughed together'
